headline: Nvidia is reportedly testing versions of its next AI processor, Rubin Ultra, with less memory than first promised because advanced memory chips are in short supply.
score_reason: Curator score 5 lowered by 1: the report appears to date from 8 Oct 2026 or earlier (Stocktwits wrote on a Thursday), before today's window, and rests on unnamed sources.
importance_line: If accurate, AI companies could need more chips, and pay more, to run the same models because memory supply is tight, but the report relies on unnamed sources and Nvidia's design choice is not final.
source: The Information, as relayed by Stocktwits
summary: Stocktwits relays a report by The Information, citing people with knowledge of the trial, that over the past few weeks Nvidia has tested at least three versions of its Rubin Ultra AI processor, some with less high-bandwidth memory (the fast memory stacked beside AI chips) than the 1 terabyte per chip announced in 2025, partly because it may not be able to buy enough of that memory. The Information says AI companies running large models on the cut-down versions might need more processors, and that the memory shortage has pushed up costs across the technology industry; the report appears to date from 8 Oct 2026 or earlier, and the article carries no comment from Nvidia.
notes: Text read is Stocktwits' retelling; The Information's own page was not read, so the url is the page where the text was read. Date of the original report not stated; 8 Oct 2026 is inferred from 'Thursday afternoon trading' in the Stocktwits text and could be earlier. Retail-trader remarks about Micron are opinion and are left out.
